mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.00% in the month preceding the decision is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 forward return due to reduced risk-free discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.00% in the prior month
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when FEDFUNDS > 5.00% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE by at least 0.25 percentage points coincides with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days, reflecting reduced labor market rigidity and improved investor sentiment.
failure_condition: In 20 consecutive windows where UNRATE rises ≥ 0.25%, the 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p ≥ 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly GDPC1 (real private consumption) exceeds INDPRO by at least 5% for two consecutive months, it predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days as it signals robust demand for capital goods.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > INDPRO by ≥ 5% for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Economic expansion with strong consumption relative to production
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not positive in 80% of such triggered windows (binomial test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in INDPRO of at least 8% followed by a rebound month later is associated with a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days as it signals supply-side weakness and short-term risk aversion.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for two consecutive months then rises in the third month
regime_hint: Supply shock or contractionary production cycle
failure_condition: In 10 such cycles, the 5-day forward return is not negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime where FEDFUNDS remains below 3.00% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 exhibits a positive 20-day forward return as expectations of future rate cuts improve equity valuations.
failure_condition: In 15 such regimes, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (t-test p ≥ 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in PAYEMS (labor market activity) of at least 10% month-over-month predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days due to market overreaction to strong labor demand.
failure_condition: Across 20 such spikes, the 60-day forward return is not consistently negative (binomial test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When monthly HOUST (housing starts) rises by at least 15% in the prior quarter, it predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days as it reflects optimism about economic recovery and credit availability.
failure_condition: In 40 such events, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (t-test p ≥ 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A double-dip in RSAFS (retail sales) with a first decline of ≥ 8% followed by a subsequent rise of ≥ 4% within the same month predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days as it signals persistent supply-side weakness and cautious investor behavior.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls ≥ 8% then rises ≥ 4% in the same month
failure_condition: In 20 such episodes, the 5-day forward return is not negative (t-test p ≥ 0.05).
